topic: What happens if you trek across polar ice?
title: What crossing polar ice does
hook: What happens if you trek across polar ice?

beats.line: The polar air is so dry that every breath pulls water out of you.
Hauling a heavy sled all day can burn about seven thousand calories.
Many polar trekkers still lose weight, even while eating huge meals.
The cold also makes you pee more, so you dry out even faster.
Snow reflects up to eighty percent of UV light, enough to sunburn your eyes.

end.line: Would you ever cross the polar ice?

description: From bone-dry air to sunburned eyes: what a trek across the polar ice does to your body.

facts.claim: Polar air holds very little water (Antarctica is the driest continent), and breathing cold, dry air increases water loss from the airways, especially during hard work.
facts.source: Institute of Medicine: Nutritional Needs in Cold and High-Altitude Environments (NCBI NBK232870) / British Antarctic Survey

facts.claim: On the 1992-93 unsupported Antarctic crossing, Stroud and Fiennes burned on average nearly 7,000 kcal a day (doubly labelled water), with stretches above 11,000 kcal on the climb to the polar plateau.
facts.source: Halsey & Stroud, Physiological Reviews 2012 (ScienceDaily summary, 12 Jun 2012)

facts.claim: Man-hauling expeditions often end with big weight loss despite huge rations: Stroud and Fiennes ate about 5,000 kcal a day and each lost over 20 kg in 95 days.
facts.source: Halsey & Stroud 2012 / UPI archives 1993 / Frykman et al., Wilderness Environ Med 2003 (Trans-Greenland)

facts.claim: Cold exposure increases urine output (cold-induced diuresis), which can add to dehydration in the cold.
facts.source: Institute of Medicine (NCBI NBK232870) / ScienceDirect Topics: cold-induced diuresis

facts.claim: Fresh snow reflects up to about 80% of UV radiation; too much UV can burn the cornea (photokeratitis, snow blindness).
facts.source: WHO (UV radiation, INTERSUN) / American Academy of Ophthalmology
